summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, systemic lupus erythematosus, interstitial lung disease, chronic diastolic heart failure, morbid obesity, and long-term anticoagulation for pulmonary embolism was admitted for worsening dyspnea on exertion, productive cough, and severe proximal myalgias. She had missed several doses of warfarin and steroids prior to admission, resulting in a subtherapeutic INR and a flare of her polymyositis, evidenced by elevated CK and troponin levels. Imaging showed mild pulmonary edema consistent with a heart failure exacerbation. She was treated with intravenous diuresis, bridged with heparin until her INR normalized on warfarin, and maintained on her baseline immunosuppressive regimen. Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation due to significant deconditioning, with plans for outpatient follow-up in cardiology and rheumatology.
